key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over months to years. LOCATION: Bilateral, diffuse. DURATION: Chronic, progressive. CHARACTER: Progressive dyspnea, dry cough. AGGRAVATING: Exertion, infections. RELIEVING: Oxygen, steroids, antifibrotics. TIMING: Chronic, progressive. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (5-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Progressive dyspnea, dry cough, fatigue, weight loss, clubbing. KEY POSITIVES: Progressive dyspnea, dry cough, clubbing. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain (unless secondary), no wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).
